doc.title: Joe Segal — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Johnny Griffin, Hampton and club life
title: Wayne takes over the business side; hotels and four-night runs
summary: He says Wayne handles licenses and money, and explains the cost of rooms and why multi-night runs beat one-nighters.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: [Laughs] Fantastic. Oh god. So now you’re, you’re of course venturing into looking or to having looking at a permanent home for the Jazz Showcase, and the challenges with that of course, and as we know, finding the right location, the economics, liquor license, all those things. You were having to negotiate them and navigate through all of that on your own, trying to figure out how to make it work.
Yeah, actually Wayne took over all the problems of that.
He’s got them handled pretty well. He’s actually the President of our corporation now.
Ok. So prior to Wayne coming in, liquor license and stuff like that. It wasn’t really part of what you had worked out?

No at the North Park we didn’t handle it at all, we had nothing to do with it. And in fact, they handled all the licensing and they also gave us rooms for the traveling musicians at the hotels, which was great. Now we’ve got all that expense on us.

Plus the rental for the room. It means we’ve got to really push, and now it’s harder and harder because there are less and less of the real playing artists that want to come and play three or four nights. They like to do these one-night concerts, get in and get out, all- star things.
And you can’t afford that, because if you have an all-star thing with a big nut and
you have a bad night, that’s it, it’s over.
You’re sunk, yeah; you’re sunk there.
This way at least with four nights we’ve got a chance.
